about: Open models Orchard's picker knows, with exact file sizes read from Hugging Face, general strength from the named public index, and scores for coding, agents, reasoning, chat and pictures from independent leaderboards that run every model the same way. Read on the date in as_of; `orchard ai pick` re-checks sizes online unless told not to. A model with no score on a leaderboard wasn't found there, which doesn't mean it is weak.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis Progress Index v1
sources.what: Read from its open-source size-class pages. Item-response-theory estimate of general capability across AA evaluations; pages /small, /medium, /large, /tiny each showed only the top 12 models, so a model missing from this list is unscored here, not necessarily low.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0.1
sources.what: Composite of several evaluations (v5 launched 27 Oct 2026, harsh: about 60% private test sets, so scores are low and not comparable with earlier versions). Whole numbers; no Coding/Agentic sub-index shown on pages read.

sources.name: SciCode (Artificial Analysis)
sources.what: SciCode: writing working scientific code for research sub-problems, scored by hidden unit tests; run by Artificial Analysis with one harness for every model. Score is the fraction solved (0 to 1). For each model the highest-effort reasoning variant that AA lists was used. Read from the model table in the page.

sources.name: AutomationBench-AA (Artificial Analysis)
sources.what: AutomationBench-AA: multi-step business workflow automation across apps (Gmail, Sheets, Slack, Salesforce, Jira and others) using tool calls, run by Artificial Analysis with one harness. Score is the partial-credit completion score (0 to 1), key 'automationbench-aa' in the embedded table. Highest-effort reasoning variant per model.

sources.name: Humanity's Last Exam (Artificial Analysis)
sources.what: Humanity's Last Exam as run by Artificial Analysis: expert-level questions needing multi-step reasoning, same harness for all models. Score is the fraction correct (0 to 1), key 'humanitys-last-exam'. Hard, so small models score near 0.04 to 0.15. Chosen over GPQA Diamond because it covers 26 of the 29 models (GPQA covers 21 and omits several of the newest large models). Highest-effort reasoning variant per model.

sources.name: LMArena Text leaderboard (style control, overall)
sources.what: Human blind pairwise preference votes on chat prompts, turned into an Elo-style rating with style control, 'overall' category. Rows read from the public Hugging Face dataset, config text_style_control, split latest, leaderboard_publish_date 2026-11-11. Rating around 1100 to 1500.

sources.name: MMMU-Pro (Artificial Analysis)
sources.what: MMMU-Pro: college-level multimodal questions with images, run by Artificial Analysis with one harness. Score is the fraction correct (0 to 1), key 'mmmu-pro'. Only models that accept images have a score. Highest-effort reasoning variant per model.

models.name: K2 Horizon 3.7B
models.notes: Maker repo file names say 4B; AA lists 3.7B. Needs llama.cpp b11454 or newer (per repo README). params_b is HF GGUF metadata (5.06B, includes embeddings); AA lists 3.7B.

models.name: Qwen3.5 4B
models.notes: No AA score read (AA listing shows only the 2B of this family in its tiny top 12).

models.name: Gemma 4 E4B
models.notes: 4.5B effective, 8B with embeddings (model card of the 12B repo family table). No AA score read.

models.name: Qwen3.5 9B
models.notes: No AA score read.

models.name: Gemma 4 12B
models.notes: Model card lists 11.95B params. No AA score read.

models.name: gpt-oss-20b
models.notes: Model card: 21B params, 3.6B active. Older (Aug 2025 release; repo updated Dec 2025). No AA score read.

models.name: Gemma 4 26B A4B
models.notes: Model card: 25.2B total, 3.8B active. No AA score read.

models.name: Qwen3.8 27B
models.notes: Dense. Scores are AA 'Xhigh' reasoning variant. Unsloth quants are the UD (dynamic) ones.

models.name: Nanbeige4.3 33B
models.notes: Top of AA small-model Progress Index list. Dense llama architecture. Repo is bartowski's, not the maker's.

models.name: Gemma 4 31B
models.notes: Dense, 30.7B. AA scores are the Reasoning variant.

models.name: Laguna XS 2.1
models.notes: Agentic coding MoE, 33B total / 3B active. Repo README still says not upstream, but its PR ggml-org/llama.cpp shows merged on 2026-07-22 (GitHub API). Only Q4_K_M and BF16 are offered; no smaller quant. No AA score read.

models.name: Qwen3.6 35B A3B
models.notes: AA score is the Reasoning variant.

models.name: K2 Horizon MoVA 36B A4B
models.notes: Maker also publishes IFM/K2-Horizon-MoVA-36B-A4B-GGUF; bartowski used here for the quant spread.

models.name: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B A3B
models.notes: AA Intelligence Index entry is 'Nemotron 3.5 Lightning'. Only Q4_0 and Q8_0 in this repo. Active 3B taken from the repo name (A3B).

models.name: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B A9B (24GB)
models.notes: Native 2-bit quantisation built to fit 24 GB; single file is the only quant. AA score is for the model family entry 'Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B'. Model card: 74B total, 9B active.

models.name: Qwen3 Coder Next 80B A3B
models.notes: Older (March 2026). Coding specialist.

models.name: gpt-oss-120b
models.notes: Native MXFP4 file, no other quant in the maker-run repo. AA entries are the High reasoning variant.

models.name: Qwen3.5 122B A10B
models.notes: AA score is the Reasoning variant.

models.name: Mistral Small 4 119B
models.notes: MoE with 128 experts, 4 active per token (model card); active parameter count not stated in the card text read, so null. AA entry is 'Mistral Small 4 Reasoning'.

models.name: Mistral Medium 3.5 128B
models.notes: Dense (AA lists no active params). HF licence field says 'other'.

models.name: Qwen3.8 Flash Next 180B A6B
models.notes: Brand new (repo updated 2026-11-13); arch 'qwen4exp'. Unsloth says run it with llama.cpp. Not in AA Intelligence Index list read.

models.name: GLM-5.3-Flash
models.notes: Native multimodal. Repo README points to a llama.cpp pull request, which GitHub shows closed and not merged; a GLM5-next code path is mentioned in other open PRs, so mainline status is unclear.

models.name: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
models.notes: Repo says it needs a llama.cpp build with M3.1 support; a llama.cpp pull request 'add MiniMax-M3.1' was still open when read.

models.name: Inkling 2 Small
models.notes: 594B total, 17B active (repo README). New 'inkling2' architecture: llama.cpp PRs / still open when read, so mainline cannot run it yet.

models.name: Ling 3.1 Flash 1019
models.notes: Repo is bartowski's, quantised with llama.cpp b11913 (so mainline supports it).

models.name: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017
models.notes: unsloth/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-GGUF returned HTTP 401 (no such repo); the 1017 update repo is used. AA lists 552B total; HF GGUF metadata counts 748.5B (not reconciled). Repo README says use unsloth's llama.cpp PR or Unsloth Desktop; llama.cpp merged PRs mention DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 so mainline support is likely but unproven. Runs on the llama.cpp release Orchard's build script uses: Orchard's own runs of the UD-IQ2_XXS files, reading from disk on one 4 core machine, gave 3.1 to 4.1 s per word.

models.name: GLM-5.3
models.notes: Model card calls it the most capable open-weights model for coding (maker's claim). Licence 'other'.

models.name: Mistral Large 4 1T A52B
models.notes: Support merged: a llama.cpp pull request closed merged 2026-10-29. AA entry 'Mistral Large 4 (High)'. Even IQ2_XXS is ~298 GB.
